title: Anchored split frames with profile-cost live reclamation: κ = 5.1414646104039e-5
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This adds a finite conditional witness with **κ = 51414646104039 / 10^18 = 5.1414646104039e-5**, a **0.7463402960%** improvement over the complete pinned PR67 witness. The scalar graph uses split vector `[1,1,2]` and moves the lowest intact global pair to the front of each common-point permutation. The compiler combines PR67 profile-cost selection with PR68 pending live controls, then scores those controls against their known next-use frame.

| Paid quantity | Pinned PR67 | This witness |
|---|---:|---:|
| h23 auxiliary roles | 27,918 | 27,455 |
| h25 auxiliary roles | 36,586 | 36,015 |
| Physical width W | 137,151,806 | 135,075,665 |
| Recursive rank mass | 78,860,441,550 | 77,666,660,475 |

The bit saving is `12854322426487/250000000000000000`. Both words include every clearing XOR, role, endpoint copy and frame raise. The complete PR67 child profile is excluded at the new bit saving; the next bit-saving and κ grid points at denominator `10^18` are also rejected. The integer profile score is a discovery heuristic; the reported saving comes from the full paid profile and exact inequalities.

The new `research/split-pair` namespace preserves contributor originals, licenses and notices. Existing numerical certificates, physical words and maintainer-reviewed statements are retained. Only the three affected root-document pins and derived certificate digests are refreshed in the older PR60 certificate; its mathematical content is identical.

Contributor credits:

- @rohangar1 (Rohan Garg): split operation in [#59](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/59).
- @ikeboy (Avi Eisenberg): interval pair graph in [#62](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/62).
- @DominikScholz (Dominik Scholz): ranked composition in [#63](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/63) and pending live controls in [#68](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/68).
- @rohanarun (Rohan Arun): schedules/refined arithmetic in [#65](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/65) and profile-cost selection in [#67](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/67).
- @eumemic: reversible compiler and physical/profile checkers in [#57](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/57).
- @chafreaky (Chafik Boukhalfa): ranked reclamation in [#60](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/60) and this aligned split/next-use-score composition.

AI assistance: this composition was prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Upstream AI-assistance disclosures remain in the preserved source notices.

PR #68's later `85781f662b57521743cce07cdd5ea194e6f3879d` concurrently combines cost and live-control ideas; this package preserves the original `734c58e` source and explicitly credits that contribution.

This remains a **finite conditional witness**. The all-size residual compiler, routing, prime selection, exact recovery, finite-alphabet/fixed-tape simulation and analytic transfer remain inherited dependencies. Arithmetic cutoffs are not full operational thresholds. No global optimality, fully formalized multiplication theorem, or measured practical speedup is claimed.

## Validation

`make -j1 split-pair-verify` **PASS**: both portable words regenerated byte-for-byte, actual profiles and exact assembly matched, and all **23 focused test methods** passed. Independent review checks the complete selected words, every input and dirty basis vector in both orientations, exact physical profiles, weighted recursive identities, pending-control eligibility, all tested complete pairings, the PR67 comparison, 47 strict assembly inequalities, seven margins, next-grid failures and source closure.

Expanded repository verification **PASS** across all eleven groups on `1bef94fd40a746452548c84a4a8f8834670a3113`, including **539 isolated tests across 80 modules** and **20 patch checks**. The initial `make -j1 verify` completed five groups before Apple clang rejected an inherited OpenMP flag; the remaining six passed with a task-local adapter to installed libomp and existing hash-verified Boost headers. The working tree remained byte-clean, and both the source-manifest and exact-certificate hashes are unchanged.

All **36 construction CI jobs passed** on that commit, including the three formal packages. The receipt-only final commit `f59cb9f54d12a2a02b665afef24a9bb5061ae011` has also [passed all 36 CI jobs](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37834000855). Independent completion review confirmed the unchanged sources and certificate, complete local coverage and exact published receipt. This PR is ready for review.
